source.title: Understanding and Mitigating Training Instability in Large-Scale Recommender Systems: A Cascade Perspective
source.authors: Yue-Ning Li; Ze-Yu Wang; Zhen Zhang; Jia-Yi Liu; Zhi-Meng Jiang; Yuji Roh; Wei-Kai Xu; Ming-Yan Gao; Onkar Dalal; Chuan He; Liang Liu

record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training-stability results for an industrial recommender, but does not test whether large networks reach near-zero training classification error or the specific conditions in V1–V6.
record.gate_note: The paper reports changes in recommender training gradients, loss, and divergence under stability interventions. These results do not measure the classification-error behavior named by the claim versions. End-task AUC and RMSE results are excluded because they are not training classification error. The listed comparisons and cited prior work are not evidence about the versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates interventions against divergence in an industrial recommender, but none of its results tests V1–V6. In particular, five-fold learning-rate stress tests do not establish rates relative to a linearized stability threshold, curvature dynamics, recovery after an initial loss rise, or edge-of-stability behavior. RMSNorm within a bundled intervention does not test batch normalization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that interventions targeting gradients, internal values or weights, and loss influence training dynamics and performance, with the combined strategy improving stability. They interpret the results as evidence of interconnected cascade components, while acknowledging that aggregated snapshots cannot validate the proposed temporal sequence for every divergence event.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates stability interventions in an industrial recommender; it does not use the claim versions' classification-error recipes or benchmark settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports stress-test outcomes for five-fold learning-rate increases and inherently unstable architectural patterns, but does not provide separate quantitative results for each condition.

fits_no_version.finding: Individual interventions reduced gradient norms by 19.6–66.7%; the combined intervention reduced them by 83.6%. Reported total-loss reductions include comparisons that replace MSE with Huber loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Targeted interventions can reduce measured gradient magnitudes in an industrial recommender; loss reductions require qualification when the objective changes.

fits_no_version.finding: The combined intervention reportedly completed training under learning-rate and architecture stress where baselines diverged, and substantially reduced clipping indicators.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A combined gradient, activation, and loss intervention can improve training robustness in the tested industrial recommender.

record.problems: The authors state that their aggregated snapshot data does not permit fine-grained temporal validation of the proposed gradient-to-weight-to-loss sequence for every divergence event. The reported changes are relative percentages without uncertainty estimates; severe-stress outcomes are described in aggregate without per-scenario values.
record.rows_left_out: End-task AUC and RMSE comparisons in Table 1 were left out because they do not measure training classification error. The stated 12 A/A arms and neutral offline/online results are not included because they do not report the claim's behavior.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large CNNs, including random or corrupted labels, and dependence on size, stopping, and regularization.
Spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation with depth, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the stated initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent training speed and trainable depth, signal and gradient propagation, and orthogonal-versus-Gaussian comparisons.
Recovery above the initial linearized stability limit, curvature reduction, divergence relative to that limit, and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics.
Batch normalization's effect on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: These rows describe the study's own intervention performance rather than evidence for V1–V6. Lack of training classification-error measurements excludes V1, but is not a general exclusion criterion for the other versions. No uncertainty estimates or scenario-specific stress-test results are supplied.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test training classification error, random or corrupted labels, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, or the stated size and training-duration conditions.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment, spurious-minimum measure, or width comparison.
No plain-versus-residual depth comparison or training classification-error measure.
No initialization comparison or signal/gradient propagation analysis across depth.
Although high-learning-rate stress tests are mentioned, the paper does not report the squared-loss stability-threshold dynamics or sharpness measures specified in this version.
No batch-normalization comparison or corresponding training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance measure.
